method: Frozen-input read-only full claim-link trace; source-specific 204-PASS audit, immutable local Git object reads, local route resolution, graph SCC classification. Graph is derived navigation, not evidence.

findings.title: Historical semantic atoms expand into full-passage PASS claims
findings.observation: VOL-C14 and BLOCKED VOL-C15 have identical current literal text about search/size plus persistence; historical claims deliberately separate these assertions. Similar payload-versus-outcome expansions affect the listed exact atoms.
findings.correction: Keep useful documentation unchanged. Make each complete current occurrence UNVALIDATED with canonical implementation plus runtime lanes; retain the old narrow static PASS as partial evidence with its exact limitation. Preserve original model record and append correction/retest. Individual proposed corrections and source-first next actions are retained on each claim.
findings.regression: Against current production inputs, assert that a PASS cannot expand the historical semantic claim into an unproven full literal. Each seven-item correction must remain UNVALIDATED with both lanes and partial evidence; VOL-C15 remains BLOCKED. A fixture that drops the runtime lane or restores PASS from only static evidence must be rejected.

findings.title: Producer contains a self-model evidence default
findings.observation: outputs() setdefault binds nonhistorical missing artifact_ref to verification/current-host-docs-review.json, and does likewise for support evidence. No current primary PASS directly uses this fallback; source inspection demonstrates a latent path, not an active circular PASS.
findings.correction: Reject missing evidence artifact_ref; do not supply the model as terminal evidence. Keep registry/model/graph references explicitly navigation or derivation only.
findings.regression: Construct a valid current evidence entry missing artifact_ref; outputs() must reject it instead of manufacturing a self reference. Also reject model, current registry, graph, prior-model-only, and summary-only terminals for runtime claims.

findings.title: Eight historical command PASS claims depend on retained sanitized execution reports
findings.observation: Reports state executed commands, dates, observations and limits. Some name hashed restricted raw files outside this isolated checkout; this audit did not access private evidence. They are reports of independent executions, not self-documentation assertions, but raw replay is unavailable here.
findings.correction: Keep explicit report-based provenance and approved restricted evidence location. Missing raw replay is not evidence the report is fabricated or runtime false.
findings.regression: Require command/execution identity and a suitable observed result, not only report status or hash; preserve restricted-evidence accessibility as a separate reviewer prerequisite.

findings.title: Computational references are separate from proof
findings.observation: The only structural SCC is the transition registry self-reference in its stored replacement evidence_refs for first-24-hours and VMs. Those references identify the correction record; independent pinned source/semantic retest and later connection observation also support the actual claim. This is bookkeeping, not confirmed self-only product proof. The model/registry/historical snapshots contain predecessor links and navigation may legitimately lead to docs in the same corpus. No direct current primary PASS artifact points to the current model or graph.
findings.correction: Publish a derived dependency graph with typed asserted_support, traced_origin, navigation_only and identity_or_history_reference edges. Flag unresolved terminals; do not count graph edges or a clean SCC result as claim proof.
findings.regression: A paired model→registry→predecessor reference with an independent runtime origin is allowed as bookkeeping; model→registry→same claim as the only alleged runtime proof must fail.

findings.title: Navigation PASS launders an embedded term-lock premise
findings.observation: All 145 navigation literal rows were manually read. This handoff alone asserts a concrete additional behavior (why terms lock at rental time), while its evidence proves only that the local destination exists. The destination repeats the assertion as an already FAIL claim with no evidence. Public agreement section captures do not establish the lock premise.
findings.correction: Keep the useful prose but make the full occurrence UNVALIDATED; preserve the original navigation PASS as partial route-existence evidence. Add implementation, runtime and authoritative-citation lanes, with an exact source-first next action rather than an automatic owner demand.
findings.regression: A resolving local link with why terms lock must not receive whole-occurrence PASS. Topic-only handoffs and question-index rows remain navigation. A documentation echo, a diagram generated from it or a graph relationship must not discharge the term-lock lane.

| Host | Publish a volume offer with the machine offer | [`vastai list machine`](/cli/reference/list-machine) |
| Host | Publish one machine's storage separately | [`vastai list volume`](/cli/reference/list-volume) |
| Host | Publish storage on several machines | [`vastai list volumes`](/cli/reference/list-volumes) |
| Host | Stop advertising a volume offer | [`vastai unlist volume`](/cli/reference/unlist-volume) |
| Renter | Find volume offers | [`vastai search volumes`](/cli/reference/search-volumes) |
| Renter | Create an owned volume from an offer | [`vastai create volume`](/cli/reference/create-volume) |
| Renter | Inspect owned volumes | [`vastai show volumes`](/cli/reference/show-volumes) |
| Renter | Link a new or existing volume to a container | [`vastai create instance`](/cli/reference/create-instance) |
| Renter | Permanently remove an unattached volume | [`vastai delete volume`](/cli/reference/delete-volume) |

claims.text:
This page has two paths. **Full system upgrade** is the shorter route for a
machine you already keep current, and it patches the kernel along with
everything else. **Kernel-only upgrade** moves the kernel and leaves the rest of
the system where it is. Neither moves Ubuntu to a newer version, for example
22.04 to 24.04.

claims.text:
A kernel upgrade only takes effect after a reboot, and a reboot stops every
running instance on the machine. Instances are not destroyed, but the workloads
inside them are interrupted. Do not start until you have a maintenance
window. Wait until all active rental contracts have ended, or schedule the
window with
[`vastai schedule maint`](/cli/reference/schedule-maint) so renters are
notified and can save their work.
